verdict.rationale: Sentry documents an official CLI (sentry-cli), but its stated scope is debug information files, release and source-map management, and code mappings, not querying or triaging Sentry data from the terminal. The AI-oriented piece is a single one-line `npx @sentry/ai install` command that teaches coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Grok) how to install Sentry; that use is evidenced only by a brief mention. Missing for 10: documented CLI commands for AI or agent workflows beyond setup (e.g., issue search or triage from the CLI), machine-readable output or agent-oriented CLI docs, and independent or hands-on corroboration of CLI use in AI-native workflows.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: It’s primarily used for managing debug information files for iOS, Android, release and source maps management, as well as code mappings for other platforms.
One command teaches Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, and Grok how to install and configure Sentry for you.
